title: A paper vocal cord (কাগজের ভোকাল কর্ড)
placement: Book pages 198–199, topic 7.3 শব্দ তরঙ্গ: next to চিত্র ৭.১০ (paper cut and folded into a vocal cord, blown between two fingers) and the নিজে করো at the foot of page 198.
description: A paper vocal cord (pages 198–199, topic 7.3, চিত্র ৭.১০ and its নিজে করো): a strip of ruled exercise-book paper folded in half, held at the foot of its crease by a small binder clip, with two flaps cut at the top of the fold, seen from above and behind the open fold the way a doctor's mirror sees the real vocal cords, on a calm blue-grey to warm backdrop. One big action, ফুঁ দাও: an outlined arrow and pale streaks of breath go down the middle of the fold, the two flaps (two paper tongues meeting at the crease) open and shut like the vocal cords, with a faint ghost at their widest swing (time slowed 100 times, said in the panel), and the sound leaves the slot as curved bands centred on it: a level slice of the air in which darker-teal compressions (সংকোচন) and lighter rarefactions (প্রসারণ) travel out while many small particles only swing in place; one green particle with a mark at its resting place shows it, and an orange bracket spans one λ between two compression centres (drawn shorter, labelled with the real value). A row of words cuts the flaps long, medium or short (14, 10, 7 mm): an honest cantilever model gives about 160, 310 and 640 Hz, so the voice goes from মোটা to তীক্ষ্ণ and λ shrinks (2.06, 1.06, 0.52 m at 330 m/s). Where the panel has room (800 × 500, 1280 × 800) a live pressure–distance graph, 0–4 m, marks a compression, a rarefaction and λ. With sound on, the buzz plays at the real frequency. The rule grows from the vocal cords to source–medium–receiver, to short = high, to the book's sentence on men's and women's voices. Test tab: 5 questions (what vibrates, what one air particle does, a shorter flap, why men's voices are deep, what sound needs), each wrong choice with its own note. Phone-first, Bangla and English.
